Let me think this through like I do every spring when I sit down with my wife and plan the year.

**My thinking:**

I have 28.1 mu total, and my main business is wheat-maize — that is what we do here in Quzhou, that is what the land knows. I will put 20 mu into the wheat-maize rotation. That gives my family our food grain and our main cash income. I know these two crops the best after 40 years. The remaining 8 mu I split among my other crops for extra income and for our own eating.

For the 20 mu of **wheat**: last year I got about 480 kg/mu and I was satisfied. I will do the same thing — 2 bags of diammonium phosphate (DAP, about 40 kg) before ploughing as base fertilizer, then 1 bag of urea (about 40 kg) per mu when the wheat greens up in spring. That gives me around 18 kg N, 8 kg P, and I add 15 kg potassium chloride for the K. The input dealer tells me potassium helps the grain fill better, and a few neighbors who added it got heavier grain, so I do it too. I will irrigate 4 times — sowing water, green-up, jointing, and grain-filling. Two sprays for aphids and rust. I use Jimai-22, an improved variety everybody here uses.

For the 20 mu of **summer maize**: I no-till directly into the wheat stubble — saves diesel and time during the busy harvest window. Denghai-605 hybrid seed, 1 bag per 3 mu. I put compound 15-15-15 at sowing, then topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage. Around 16 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. One irrigation if the rains don't come, one spray for borer. I expect about 580 kg/mu.

For **cotton (3 mu)**: cotton is fussy and needs many sprays — aphids and bollworm never stop. I use Bt cotton seed. Plough in spring, base fertilizer heavier on potassium because cotton loves potassium for the bolls. About 14 kg N, 6 kg P, 7 kg K. I will spray 6 times — no way around it. Irrigate 3 times.

For **chrysanthemum (2 mu)**: this is a cash crop, sells well to the tea buyers. I keep fertilizer moderate — too much N and the flowers lose quality. 10 kg N, 6 kg P, 7 kg K. Rotary till, improved variety. 3 sprays for aphids and leaf miner.

For **soybean (1.5 mu) and mungbean (1 mu)**: these fix their own nitrogen, so I only put a little starter fertilizer. Mostly for our own eating and a small sale.

For **spinach (0.6 mu)**: kitchen vegetable, autumn planting after maize. Needs water and nitrogen.

Overall I spend a bit more on fertilizer than some of my neighbors — I would rather spend the extra 50 yuan/mu than lose 100 kg of grain. A good harvest pays everything back; a bad one ruins the year.
